_comment.about: The Next.js half of the delivery product (delivery/frappe is the Frappe half: parcel orders, delivery points and zones, deliveryman profiles and settings, dispatch routes, intercity providers, tips, reviews and weather notices, with the 47 whitelisted API methods manifest.json lists). Ray, 2026-09-09: the delivery-platform landing "will be selling a delivery platform not selling to merchants, his portal is the one that sell to merchants" - so this SDK is BOTH the storefront that sells the platform to whoever will run one and the door to the tenant portal that a tenant's own domain opens. It is the delivery shell's home SDK (RokctAI/delivery-frontend, app_type deliveryplatform; core/utils/frappe/composer/deliveryplatform.json flags it home_sdk: true beside base_sdk, auth_sdk, telemetry_sdk and the commerce portal SDKs; no agent_sdk, whose integrations are unconditional and flip the shell AI-first), so it owns the root route and fills every seam base_sdk's landing host offers with ONE registered module each. The root route is app/(chat)/page.tsx, NOT app/page.tsx as hosting_sdk's and lms_sdk's are: the delivery-frontend shell keeps its holding copy of `/` there (its comment: moving it to app/page.tsx would leave two "/" routes at compose time), so installing there overwrites the shell copy, the way base_sdk's host files overwrite theirs. A signed-in session goes to base_sdk's manager shell at /manager (the paas-era /paas/dashboard, which base_sdk >= 1.2.0 carries as app/manager/*); a visitor naming a tenant (?site_name=) or arriving on a tenant's own domain (base's tenant-host lookup, ROKCT_TENANT_HOSTS or a registered resolver) gets auth_sdk's PaaSLogin; everyone else is redirected to the composed landing at /landing. app/paas/dashboard/page.tsx and app/paas/admin/page.tsx keep the paas-era paths answering (auth_sdk 1.6.0's auth.config.ts still falls back to them for a PaaS login whose backend names no homePage) by forwarding to /manager and /admin. The landing seams: components/custom/landing/delivery-hero-copy.ts at // @rokct-sdk-hero-copy-start (base_sdk >= 1.6.0; the two delivery services and driver dispatch cycle as the headline, the suffix is the plan fixtures' white-label line, the trust line the two facts the two PaaS plan records share), delivery-hero-form.tsx at // @rokct-sdk-hero-form-start (base_sdk >= 1.7.0; two calls to action and no input: the pricing section and the login, LANDING_CONFIG.loginUrl, because the storefront sells the platform and a tenant's people sign in to the portal from here), delivery-features-section.tsx, delivery-apps-section.tsx and delivery-pricing-section.tsx at // @rokct-sdk-page-sections-start (base_sdk >= 1.11.0; the pricing section declares meta.renders over the prefetched rows so the section and its Pricing nav stop drop together when the control site returns none, and strips the inline markup the PaaS fixtures' first feature line carries), delivery-header-menu.ts at // @rokct-sdk-header-menu-start (base_sdk >= 1.21.0; three anchors, features, apps and pricing, and ONE group of three app cards the way lms 1.12.0 added its "Get the app" cards, drawn as cards by base_sdk >= 1.18.0; no actions because base's header already draws Log in and Sign up; since 1.0.1 `brand: { logo: "none" }`, base_sdk >= 1.21.0's HeaderMenu.brand, the way lms_sdk 1.13.0 declares it - Ray, 2026-09-09: "let home sdk declare if it needs logo there or not"; juvo has no icon yet, so the header draws the wordmark alone and no image in the brand slot), delivery-site-metadata.ts at // @rokct-sdk-site-metadata-start (base_sdk >= 1.15.0; its own SiteMetadataCopy-shaped interface, no icon so base_sdk >= 1.17.0's generated letter favicon applies; siteName "juvo" and url https://juvo.app, Ray 2026-09-09: "deliveryplatform will be juvo so i will point juvo.app to it"), and delivery-plans-query.ts at // @rokct-sdk-plans-query-start (base_sdk >= 1.9.0; LANDING_CONFIG.plansQuery with ONE filter laid over its payload, ["plan_category", "=", "paas"], the inclusive mirror of agent_sdk 1.10.0's exclusion; no plan id or name anywhere in the filter). Their copy is components/custom/landing/delivery-page-sections.ts and the hero and metadata modules; the apps section (Ray, 2026-09-09: "deliveryplatform will show off three apps paas_customer, paas_manager, paas_driver as customer, manager, delivery apps with downloads and demo account details for potentials to try them") reads components/custom/landing/delivery-apps.ts, lms 1.12.0's LMS_APPS shape: one entry per app in Ray's order with a `shown` flag per build (Android from every repo's release lane, Windows from paas_manager's only, iOS shown: false everywhere - "ios is demoted for now"), every href the repo's releases/latest page, each description the app's own feature-guide line; its try-it block renders ONLY from environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_JUVO_DEMO_SITE and NEXT_PUBLIC_JUVO_DEMO_{CUSTOMER,MANAGER,DRIVER}_LOGIN / _PASSWORD, inlined at build time) and hides itself while they are unset, because the demo-account mechanism the apps carry (users_sdk 1.3.8's is_demo_account marker, auth_sdk 1.11.0 / base_sdk 1.61.0's DemoSession) seeds no account - an operator marks one - so no source spells a login and this SDK writes none; every claim is a fact from zones/delivery/docs (the terms and the intercity provider design), zones/delivery/frappe (the manifest's whitelisted API and the doctypes), the PaaS plan fixtures in commerce/merchants/frappe/src/tenant/fixtures/Subscription_Plan (the feature lines, USD, Monthly and Yearly, the 14-day trial on the yearly record) or the paas_driver and paas_manager feature guides, and nothing a source does not carry is said. Colours route through the shell's theme tokens, never a literal brand colour. The portal: components/custom/nav/delivery-nav.tsx is the deliveryman's sidebar group base_sdk's app-sidebar.tsx imports and gates and names in its `requires` as the delivery frontend's to take; its entries sit under /manager as merchants_sdk 1.1.0's merchant-nav.tsx entries do. The shell's other portal files are NOT shipped because base_sdk or auth_sdk already own them: app-sidebar.tsx (base's has the same role gating and imports this nav), nav/admin-nav.tsx (base's, pointing at its /admin pages), nav/merchant-nav.tsx (merchants_sdk's), app/paas/dashboard/layout.tsx (base's app/manager/layout.tsx), app/lib/session.ts and the auth seams (auth_sdk's); app/lib/paas-gateway.ts is a one-line hand-off to the kernel's paasCall (base_sdk >= 1.3.0). Floors: base_sdk >= 1.21.0 (HeaderMenu.brand, which delivery-header-menu.ts declares since 1.0.1 and which is a type error in the registry's HeaderMenu against 1.18.0-1.20.0; the home_sdk composer, protocol #390, shipped with 1.19.0; every registry this SDK targets exists from 1.15.0, the generated favicon from 1.17.0), auth_sdk >= 1.6.0 (PaaSLogin, the session seam and the tenant-link registry), telemetry_sdk (every Next.js composition). base_sdk composes first, auth_sdk before this SDK because the root route renders its PaaSLogin and the landing's login and sign-up links are its routes. The register page stays auth_sdk's: auth_sdk 1.7.0 is turning register into a registry the home SDK fills, and the delivery registration (provisioning on the control site) is the follow-up once it lands. The tenant admin surface (1.1.0): app/admin/logistics/location-types/page.tsx maintains the vocabulary a driver files a point of interest against - every Location Type with the active points filed under it, a shown-to-customers switch per type, the seeded badge, an add-a-type form, and the free texts drivers typed under the catch-all type with the one action that promotes a recurring one and re-types its points. It sits under /admin/logistics, where base_sdk's admin nav already keeps the delivery pages (zones, vehicles, deliveryman settings), and reads and writes ONLY map's five api.poi.admin_* whitelisted defs through base_sdk >= 1.3.0's kernel paasCall (app/actions/delivery/admin/location-types.ts): admin_list_location_types, admin_create_location_type, admin_set_type_visibility, admin_list_custom_types and admin_promote_custom_type. Those defs assert the roles themselves (System Manager or Administrator), so the page adds no gate of its own. components/custom/nav/delivery-admin-nav.tsx is the sidebar group for it, registered by two integrations lines on base_sdk's app-sidebar.tsx rather than by shipping a copy of base's 380-line nav/admin-nav.tsx: an import beside the DeliveryNav import this SDK already owns, and the gated render after <SidebarContent>, both literals read from base_sdk 1.47.0. The installer skips an integration whose placeholder is absent, so an older or rearranged sidebar simply draws no group and the pages stay reachable by URL. The page is inert until map's POI API lands: until then every call answers with the gateway's failure and the page shows its could-not-load state.

_comment.app/services/base/session.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.3.0 (getPlatformSession, the kernel session seam app/(chat)/page.tsx reads)

_comment.components/custom/landing/hero-copy.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.6.0 (the hero copy registry the delivery-hero-copy integration targets; HeroCopy for delivery-hero-copy.ts)
_comment.components/custom/landing/hero-form.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.7.0 (the hero body registry the delivery-hero-form integration targets; HeroFormProps for delivery-hero-form.tsx)
installed by base_sdk >= 1.11.0 (the registry the two section integrations target; PageSectionMeta/PageSectionProps for the section templates; >= 1.11.0 because delivery-pricing-section.tsx declares PageSectionMeta.renders)

installed by base_sdk >= 1.15.0 (the site-metadata registry the delivery-site-metadata integration targets; delivery-site-metadata.ts imports nothing from it, so against an older base the installer only skips the line)
